q: What relationship does John have with Gaius, the one receiving this letter?
For what does John pray concerning Gaius?
a: John prays that Gaius would prosper in everything and be in health, as his soul prospers.
John’s greatest joy is to hear that his children are walking in the truth.
Gaius worked for the brothers even though they were strangers.

q: How should Gaius send the brothers on?
a: He should sent them on worthily of God.

q: Why did the brothers need help from the believers to send them out on their journey?
a: They needed help because they were not accepting anything from the Gentiles.

q: Why does John say believers should welcome such people?
a: John says believers should welcome them to become fellow-workers with the truth.
Diotrephes loves to be first among the people of his church.

q: What is Diotrephes’ attitude toward John?
What will John do when he comes to Gaius and the congregation?
a: When John comes, he will call attention to the works that Diotrephes is doing.

q: What does Diotrephes do with the brothers who are sent out?
a: Diotrephes does not receive these brothers.

q: What does Diotrephes do with those who are willing to receive these brothers?
a: Diotrephes stops them from receiving the brothers and puts them out of the church.

q: What does John tell Gaius to imitate?
a: John tells Gaius to imitate what is good.

q: What does John expect to do in the future?
a: John expects to come and speak with Gaius in person.
